patch_description: This crossover combines the best elements of both parents: (1) the gradient-based SLSQP smooth-minimum optimizer from the inspiration program (which is effective but slow due to a Python-loop Jacobian), and (2) the fast vectorized min-area evaluation and stochastic hill-climbing refinement from the current program. Key improvements: the Jacobian is fully vectorized with `np.add.at` (removing the 165-triplet Python loop), fewer starts are used with an iteration budget to keep runtime reasonable, a deterministic stochastic polish phase (single- and two-point moves with clipping) refines the SLSQP output to escape soft-min bias, and the fallback path now uses a verified distinct-point lattice so the result never degenerates to zero area even if optimization fails. Feasibility is guaranteed by final projection into the triangle.
